text.p: Hollinger Inc said on Wednesday that it amended a bid to acquire the shares of Southam Inc it did not already own, winning the approval of a special Southam committee.

Hollinger said each Hollinger special share offered in exchange would now be denominated in U.S. instead of Canadian dollars and be exchangeable into class A Hollinger International shares over a three-year period. Southam's special committee, established to consider the offer, said it would recommend acceptance of the amended offer to Southam's board of directors.
Hollinger originally offered C$23.50 a share, split into C$13.50 in cash and C$10 in the form of a Hollinger Canadian non-voting special share.
The amended shares will be exchangeable on the following basis after the offer expires:
Exchange Period Number of Class A Shares
1. between 6 and 12 months 0.51
2. thereafter, within 18 months 0.53
3. thereafter, within 24 months 0.55
4. thereafter, within 30 months 0.57
5. thereafter but prior to the
date which is two weeks before
the automatic exchange date 0.59
6. thereafter but prior to the
automatic exchange date 0.602.

If the special shares are not exchanged, they will be automatically rolled over on the first business day three years after offer expires. The exchange will be on the basis of a ratio calculated by dividing $8.88 (C$12.31) by 95 percent of the then weighted average trading price of Class A Shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Hollinger International shares slipped 3/8 to 11-1/2 in light dealings on the New York Stock Exchange. In Toronto, trading was halted in Southam, which last traded down 0.15 to 22.55 in thin turnover.
Hollinger Canadian already owns a 50.45 percent stake in Southam.
Southam's board is expected to approve a circular on June 13 that will recommend shareholders accept the amended bid.
On June 12, Hollinger Canadian will mail to Southam shareholders a note with the amended offer and will extend its expiry to June 23, 1900 EDT/2300 GMT from June 18.
A special meeting of Southam shareholders was rescheduled to 1100 EDT/1500 GMT on June 23 from June 18.
The companies applied to list the special shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Hollinger also said: "The exchange ratios set out above are calculated on the basis of an assumed market price for the Class A Shares of $14.75."
"As a result, if the market price of the Class A Shares exceeds $14.75 during the option period, holders may decide that it is in their economic interest to exercise the exchange right."

"For example, if the market price of the Class A Shares were $18.00 per share during the last optional exchange period, for each exchangeable share exchanged, the holder would receive 0.602 X $18.00 (or) $10.84, worth of Class A Shares which is equivalent to approximately C$15.00 based on current foreign exchange rates."

"Hollinger International will have the option to satisfy its exchange obligation on any optional exchange by a cash payment for all or any portion of each exchangeable share to be exchanged in U.S. dollars equal to the then current market price of the Class A Shares that would be issuable on exchange."

"The terms of the exchangeable shares will also be amended to include additional events which will cause acceleration of the automatic exchange date and an undertaking by Hollinger Canadian to obtain, within six months after the expiry of the offer, credit ratings for the exchangeable shares from recognized rating agencies."
